title: Universal-certificate characterization of coNP
statement: For every language $L$ of binary strings, $L$ belongs to coNP if and only if there are natural numbers $C,c$ and a language $V$ in polynomial time such that, for every binary string $x$, membership $x\in L$ is equivalent to the condition that every binary string $u$ of length exactly $C(|x|+1)^c$ satisfies $xu\in V$, where $xu$ is the concatenation of $x$ and $u$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of binary strings
replaced:
A language $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^{*}$ belongs to the class coNP (that is, its
complement lies in $\mathsf{NP}$) if and only if there exist natural numbers $C$ and
$c$ and a verifier language $V \in \mathsf{P}$ such that for every binary string $x$,
\[
  x \in L \iff \text{for every } u \in \{0,1\}^{*} \text{ with } |u| = C \cdot (|x|+1)^{c},\ \ xu \in V,
\]
where $xu$ denotes the concatenation of $x$ and $u$.
